intended_object: The quotient u_r/r (radial velocity component divided by the distance r to the symmetry axis) of an axisymmetric vector field in ℝ³ × time, taken on the meridional plane {x₂ = 0} and extended continuously across the axis by its limit ∂₁u₁. This comes from the docstring and from how the CIV axisymmetric regularity files use it.
explanation:
The definition returns u₁/x₁ when x₁ ≠ 0. When x₁ = 0 it returns ∂₁u₁, the spatial partial derivative given by `fderiv` along e₀ at fixed time.

On a meridional point (x₁, 0, x₃) with x₁ > 0, we have r = x₁ and u_r = u₁. When x₁ < 0, r = −x₁ and u_r = −u₁, so u₁/x₁ = u_r/r there as well. So the off-axis branch is exactly u_r/r on the whole plane, as the library's reflection lemma `radialQuotient_reflect` also uses.

On the axis, an axisymmetric smooth field has u₁(0, 0, x₃) = 0. The limit of u₁/x₁ as x₁ → 0 is therefore ∂₁u₁, which is the standard continuous extension the manuscript describes. The library proves this continuity in `continuousOn_radialQuotient_plane`.

The function is defined at every point of space-time, but its value means u_r/r only on the meridional plane. The docstring says so ("read on the meridional plane"), and every use in the library evaluates it at `meridional x₁ x₃`. Its values off the plane are irrelevant, not an error.

The quantity is specific to axisymmetric flows in ℝ³, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no counterpart.
